relevance_note: Single case report of a boy with a TNFAIP3 variant: 'a novel de novo heterozygous 2 bp deletion in tumour necrosis factor-alpha-induced protein 3 (TNFAIP3, figure 1A)'.
method_note: Read the paper in full and built the JSON with a short Python script in my scratch directory; values were chosen by reading, and table-row spans were copied from the file (the 'Activated T cells' row contains an em space). One in-scope person, labelled 'patient' (single unnamed patient of a case report; the figure legend calls him 'patient (P)'). Table 1 columns are timepoints (Pretransplant / Post-transplant) for this one patient, not different patients; pretransplant values used for details. Relatives: the parents ('healthy non-consanguineous British parents'), healthy siblings and a first-born infant who died of prematurity are mentioned (text and figure 1A legend) but are neither described as tested nor affected, so they get no rows. Inheritance: the paper calls the variant 'de novo' but does not describe parental testing, so under rule 8 inheritance and parental_testing_statement are 'not reported'. Variant notation differs within the paper: 'c.1466_1467delTG' / 'p.V489Afs*7' in the text versus 'c.1466_1467TGdel' / 'V489Afs*7' in the figure 1 legend; the text form was recorded. Age at last evaluation '14-year-old' is the age at investigation; the latest status is 21 months post-transplant and no later age is given. Numeric laboratory values in Table 1 outside reference ranges (e.g. haemoglobin, platelets, IgM, IgA, CD19+, FEV_1) were not turned into features unless the text or table names the finding; they were not linked to specific features. Checklist items 'gastrointestinal ulcers or inflammation', 'autoimmune hepatitis' and 'cytopenia (autoimmune)' were marked observed from 'enteropathy', 'hepatitis' and 'cytopaenias' listed as components of 'complex autoimmunity'. 'No other autoantibodies were detected' was recorded as an excluded feature but does not exclude the autoantibody checklist item (anti-GAD, islet cell antibody and pANCA were detected). STAT3 and FOXP3 were reported as excluded genetically; no variants in other genes recorded. No contradictions about phenotypes found.

clinical_diagnosis_basis.value: Genetic testing: whole exome sequencing with bioinformatic filtering, variant confirmed by capillary (Sanger) sequencing, with functional validation in patient fibroblasts; STAT3 and FOXP3 variants excluded
span: By whole exome sequencing of peripheral blood genomic DNA (Illumina MiSeq) and downstream bioinformatic filtering (Ingenuity Variant Analysis), we identified a single biologically plausible variant
The c.1466_1467delTG variant—which we confirmed by capillary sequencing10 (figure 1B)
Pathogenic variants in STAT3 and FOXP3 were excluded
Here we provide novel validation of considerable existing evidence that implicates TNFAIP3 in autoimmune pathogenesis

variant_type_as_stated.span: identifying a single heterozygous frameshift variant in TNFAIP3

zygosity.span: a novel de novo heterozygous 2 bp deletion

functional_evidence_statement.value: Reduced basal and TNF-induced A20 protein in patient fibroblasts (immunoblot); exaggerated and prolonged NF-kB pathway phosphorylation after TNF-alpha; increased range and magnitude of TNF-alpha-stimulated gene expression (RNA-seq); enhanced IL-6 protein by ELISA; molecular consequences indistinguishable from reported pathogenic A20 mutations
span: Immunoblotting10 of patient and control dermal fibroblast lysates with an N-terminal antibody confirmed the reduced basal and TNF-α-induced expression of A20 (figure 1D)
We observed exaggerated and prolonged phosphorylation of components of the NF-κB pathway
RNA sequencing (Illumina NextSeq-500) revealed a significant global increase in both the range and magnitude of TNF-α-stimulated differential gene expression
We also confirmed enhanced expression of the key NF-κB target gene interleukin 6 (IL-6) at the protein level by ELISA (p=0.0015, figure 1G)
the molecular consequences of the p.V489Afs*7 variant were indistinguishable from reported pathogenic A20 mutations
a heterozygous loss-of-function mutation in TNFAIP3 (A20)
a novel de novo heterozygous 2 bp deletion
